Commentary.Commentary: So, the target for West Indies is a mere 144 in the 50 overs. Can South Africa replicate the efforts of the West Indian bowlers? Or will they end up on the losing side? Do join us on the other side of the break for the run chase.

Talking of the South African batting, it was a sorry tale as it has been throughout the tournament. Only shining light for them was Levert Manje who showed some fight. But once he departed the downfall started. The young heads of South Africa hit the panic button and looked lost in the process. Wickets falling at regular intervals impacted their momentum too. They also lacked the application to play the pacers as well as the spinners despite knowing the ground and conditions better than the team from West Indies.

A brillant effort with the ball for the colts from the Carribean. They were spot on from the word go. The pacers especially Jayden Seales was on fire. He kept peppering the South African batsmen every now and then and that helped to create the pressure on the Saffas. Joshua James in particular was lethal as he was generating a lot of extra bounce and that also troubled the batsmen. When the spinners came in, it was superb from them. They did not let the pressure created by the pacers early on to fade. Ashmead Nedd was class apart as he got lot of bounce and turn from the pitch. Not to forget, the fielding placements and captaincy was superb.

OUT! CAUGHT! The catch is taken this time. Full and outside off, van Vuuren looks to play the slog but does not quite time it cleanly. Joshua James at deep mid-wicket gets down on a knee and takes it calmly. WEST INDIES NEED 144 TO WIN!
DROPPED! The fielder overran it. Full and outside off, van Vuuren gets down to play the slog sweep but mistimes it towards long on. The fielder runs back but then fumbles. The batsmen do not run.
Patrick is back on.
Modimokoane looks to run this length ball down to third man but he fails to find the gap as short third man cuts it off there.
Odirile Modimokoane walks in as the last man.

OUT! CAUGHT! Cloete is the latest addition in the list of casualties. He tries to play like his partner but cannot imitate him. A short ball outside off, coming too with the angle. Cloete goes for a cut shot over point. But he gets it off the higher part of the bat and the ball lobs towards covers where Ashmead Nedd takes a dolly running to his left a bit.
Slower and outside off, Cloete looks to run that through third man but he gets beaten on the outside edge there.
Full and outside off, Cloete plays it with an angled bat and runs it down towards third man. There is no one manning that area and the ball goes to the fence.

In the air... Just over the fielder at covers. James bowls one on a length and Cloete lofts it cleanly over covers. The man there jumps in the air but the ball goes over him and towards deep cover. The batsmen get a couple.
Short and outside off, van Vuuren cuts it uppishly over point and gets a run.
Joshua James is back on. 6-1-18-1 are his figures so far.
Van Vuuren drives this fuller one through covers and retains the strike here.
Fuller and on middle and leg, van Vuuren plays it off the back foot and towards the leg side.
Full and around off, pushed to mid off by the batsman.
Fuller and on middle and leg, van Vuuren tucks it towards fine leg and gets a couple with ease.
Flatter and outside off, van Vuuren drives it to covers.
Fuller and on off, defended to the off side.

Full and down the leg side and the batsman misses the flick.
Length ball outside off, van Vuuren plays it toward point.
Full and outside off, pushed towards the bowler.

A bumper and van Vuuren looks to duck it but the ball hits the arm and lobs towards the slip cordon. The fielder there pouches it and appeals only for the umpire to say it not out. The replays confirm that the umpire's decision is the right one.

Floated delivery on middle, van Vuuren blocks it well.
Tossed up delivery on off, van Vuuren plays it to point.
BEATEN AGAIN! Loopy delivery outside off, van Vuuren looks to cut but misses it.
BEATEN! Floated delivery just outside off, Tiaan looks to defend but misses it.
Flighted delivery on middle, van Vuuren blocks it off the back foot.
Tossed up delivery on off, van Vuuren defends it off the front foot.

OUT! RUN OUT! South Africa are falling like nine pins here. Another miscommunication and a casualty occurs. Patrick tosses one up a bit fuller and outside off, Brett drives it towards cover-point and takes off for a run. His partner is not at all watching him and is unresponsive to his call. Merrick Brett sees the fielder from covers pounce on the ball and release it towards the keeper. He turns and runs behind and puts in a dive also. But by then the keeper Julian had already shattered the stumps. The umpire though to be sure takes it upstairs and the replays later show that Brett was short of his ground there.
An appeal for run out! It is referred upstairs. Replays show that Merrick Brett is out.

Full and down the leg side once again, Brett looks to flick it towards fine leg but the ball hits the pads and goes towards the leg side.
Full and on off, pushed off the front foot towards mid off.
Full and down the leg side, Brett looks to flick but misses it and the ball rolls off the pads towards mid on.
Floated and around off, Brett presses forward and blocks it right under his eyes.
On off, van Vuuren defends it out.
Loopy delivery on middle, Brett flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
Flighted delivery on middle, Brett blocks it off the front foot.

NOT OUT! Brett is safe. Tossed up delivery just outside off, Brett looks to defend but misses it. It goes towards the keeper where Julien takes the bails off. It is referred upstairs. The replays show that his foot is well inside the crease.
An appeal for stumping! Merrick Brett is the man in question. It is referred upstairs. The replays come in and Brett is fine as his feet go nowhere when the bails get dislodged.
Floated delivery on off, Brett keeps it out.

OUT! Stumped! Nedd gets his second wicket. Flighted delivery just outside off, Cotani comes down the track and looks to defend but misses it. It goes towards the keeper where Julien takes the bails off.
Loopy delivery on off, Tiaan plays it to point.

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! Oh! Patrick starts to celebrate as soon as he took the catch. The umpires though are not sure and then converge to go upstairs. The soft signal is out and now the replays roll in to show that Moletsane has to go back to the hut here. Patrick bowls one fuller and on middle and leg, Moletsane looks to go down town by dancing down the track but he fails to get to the pitch of the ball. The bat turns in his hand on impact and the bat hits the ground. That is why the ball lobs straight to the bowler who takes it with  both hands and starts celebrating.
Is that a return catch? The batsman is going nowhere. The umpires get together and refer it upstairs. The soft signal is OUT. Here comes the replay. It is a catch!
Full and spinning in, Molestane comes on the front foot and keeps it out.
Flighted and around off, Molestane defends it to covers off the front foot.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.

DRINKS BREAK. The wicket could not have come at a better time for the Windies. They are applying pressure now and are into the lower middle order. Another wicket and we could see the innings hastening itself to completion.

OUT! CLEANED UP! Nedd beat him in the last ball of the last over and this time  he has his man. He tosses one up on middle and leg, Lees goes for the flick towards the leg side. Full and off, pushed off the back foot towards the bowler.

OUT! CAUGHT! Straight to the man! Catching practice. How much of that is influenced by the man under the helmet at short leg? No, not by sledging. But because of that man present right under his nose, Beaufort tried to manufacture a shot. He wants to go inside out. And James bowls it 6 inches outside off, short in length. Beaufort has to reach out and try to cut. Ends up hitting it straight to Kimani Melius at point! He cannot believe what he has done.

Is that reverse? Naah... cannot be this early. Beaufort backs away down the leg side and James follows him, bowling an inswinger. He misses his flick, does the batsman, due to too much swing and is hit on the pads.
Drinks Break! Going at a decent rate, are South Africa, but the boundaries seem to have dried up. However, they would do well to keep wickets in hand and just forge a partnership.

FOUR! Cracking shot. Short and outside off, Beaufort cuts it over point. Jayden Seales runs hard to his right from third man, gets to the ball, pushes it back in, goes beyond the boundary, comes back in, tries to stop but by then it is too late. The ball has touched the ropes. Great effort though.

Bowls a bouncer, Manje does well to duck under it.
BEATEN! On a good length and outside off, Manje looks to defend but misses it.

Another rip snorter! Wow. Seales is on fire. Nearly gets two in two. he bowls a quick short delivery on off, Manje looks to fend but again, the ball just kicks up after pitching. It hits the glove and then lobs in the air. First slip gets across to his right, dives but cannot get there! A single taken.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! That is a rip snorter! But Parsons does not want to go. He is on his haunches when the finger goes up in appeal and is shaking his head. He stays there looking at the umpire in dismay. Did he not nick it? A tough, tough call according to the replays. But what a brute of a nut. This is pitched on a good length, around leg, Parsons looks to defend but the ball kicks up after pitching and goes past him, to the keeper. That is what we feel. The fielding side appeals and the umpire raises his finger! We are shown just one replay and Tom Moody feels that the ball has grazed the glove. If he is saying it, there might have been but really difficult for an onlooker to judge that.
On a good length on middle, Parsons defends it to mid-wicket.

WIDE. Full and down the leg side, Manje misses his flick.

It is time for the national anthems. West Indies' first. We are all set for the game to begin. The players are back out on the field. Jonathan Bird and Levert Manje are the openers for the Proteas. Jayden Seales to bowl with the first new ball. Bird to face. Here we go!

WEST INDIES SKIPPER, KIMANI MELIUS, says that he would have batted first but now that they are bowling, the pacers would look to take some early wickets. On the previous match's loss, the captain says that it is time to move on and perform well against South Africa today.

SOUTH AFRICAN CAPTAIN, BRYCE PARSONS, says that the decision to bat first is because they struggled early in the morning but wants his side to weather the storm today and play well. Is disappointed with the way their tournament ended and just wants to end it in a nice manner now. On learnt lessons, Parsons reckons that South Africa are going the right way for the future and just need to be persistent and believe in themselves.

PITCH REPORT - Pommie Mbangwa has a look at the surface and observes a bit of green on it. JP Duminy is reminded of a good Day 1 Test wicket, which means, it looks like a good batting surface but the first hour will give you good amount of lateral movement and carry. He reckons that there is a pretty good covering of live grass on the wicket.

West Indies U19 (Playing XI) - Kimani Melius (C), Leonardo Julien (WK), Kevlon Anderson, Kirk Mckenzie, Antonio Morris, Matthew Patrick, Nyeem Young, Joshua James, Ashmead Nedd, Jayden Seales, Ramon Simmonds (In for Matthew Forde).

South Africa U19 (Playing XI) - Jonathan Bird, Khanya Cotani (WK), Bryce Parsons (C), Luke Beaufort, Merrick Brett (In for Tyrese Karelse), Tiaan van Vuuren, Jack Lees, Pheku Moletsane, Achille Cloete, Levert Manje (In for Gerald Coetzee) and Odirile Modimokoane (In for Mondli Khumalo).
TOSS - Heads is the call from the West Indies skipper, Tails it is. SOUTH AFRICA WILL BAT FIRST.

Hello and welcome to the 5th place playoff between West Indies and South Africa. West Indies would be the most disappointed side of the two after being one of the favourites to lift the trophy and then crash out of the semi-finals' race. South Africa were not at their best throughout the tournament. West Indies are the favourites and South Africa need to come out attacking if they are to win the game against the Carribeans.
